subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Aerodynamics
description: A micro-lesson that makes Aerodynamics usable.

hook.text: At highway speed, a car spends more energy fighting air than fighting its own weight.

buildup.text: Air resistance (drag) rises with the square of speed. Going twice as fast means four times the drag.

discovery.text: A drag coefficient measures how slippery a shape is. A brick is about 2.1. A Tesla Model 3 is 0.23.

twist.text: Flat underbodies, tapered tails, and sealed grilles save real fuel—or add miles to EV range.

climax.text: Race cars add wings to create downforce—pushing the car into the road for more grip at speed.

punchline.text: Air is invisible but never free to push through.

quiz.question: How does drag change when speed doubles?
